content: The cost of waste handling is calculated per safety training session. The cost of developing codes and standard operating procedures is also considered. Guidelines for costing tuberculosis (TB) interventions are provided, detailing intervention classes, specific intervention details, and the associated technology platforms. The population targeted by these interventions is specified, and standard unit costs are calculated for both direct and ancillary services. TB policy, planning, coordination, and management activities include the development of strategic plans, program reviews, national and regional meetings, supervision, management and information systems, surveys, procurement and supply chain management, advocacy, technical assistance, training, laboratory accreditation and quality assurance, specimen transport, community media, information, education, and communication efforts, as well as partnership activities. These activities are carried out by national TB programs, ministries of health, public and private health facilities, non-governmental organizations, healthcare workers, and laboratory staff. Costs are broken down into program management costs, activity unit costs, training costs, software development costs, event costs, workshop costs, supervisory visit costs, and item transportation costs. Specific TB-related terms and technologies are defined, such as Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB), rifampicin (RIF), light-emitting diode (LED), Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), cluster of differentiation 4 (CD4), line probe assay (LPA), first-line drugs (FLD), second-line drugs (SLD), drug-susceptibility testing (DST), loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP), lateral flow urine lipoarabinomannan assay (LF-LAM), interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA), tuberculin skin test (TST), purified protein derivative (PPD), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase (SGOT), random blood sugar (RBS), polymerase chain reaction-deoxyribonucleic acid (PCR-DNA), extra-pulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB), computed tomography (CT), electrocardiography (ECG), maternal child health (MCH), drug-sensitive TB (DS-TB), multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB), pre-extensively drug-resistant TB (Pre-XDR-TB), extensively drug-resistant TB (XDR-TB), public-private mix (PPM), practical approach to lung health (PAL), mobile health (M-health), antiretroviral therapy (ART), drug-resistant TB (DR-TB), directly observed treatment (DOT), 6-month isoniazid (6H), and once-weekly isoniazid-rifapentine for 12 weeks (3HP). The World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines do not recommend IGRA for detecting latent TB infection, but it is used in some settings. Costing studies should follow principles and methods outlined by the Global Health Cost Consortium (GHCC). These include defining the type of cost (economic vs. financial, real-world vs. guideline, full vs. incremental), specifying the time horizon, and ensuring the scope of inputs is justified. Methods for estimating input quantities, sampling strategies, and data sources should be described, and potential biases should be reported. The timing of data collection should minimize recall bias and account for seasonality. Price data sources should be listed, distinguishing between local and international sources. Statistical methods for analyzing cost differences and determinants should be described. Uncertainty in cost estimates should be characterized through sensitivity analyses, and limitations in design, analysis, and results should be transparently communicated. Ethical considerations include informed consent, confidentiality, and community engagement. Study protocols should outline objectives, study design, data management, and expected applications of results. Appendices provide additional details, such as budget summaries, intervention descriptions, and investigator roles. Specific interventions include vaccination, intensified case finding, active and passive case finding, TB treatment, latent TB infection treatment, infection prevention control, and TB policy and management. The Value TB Costing Tool Suite includes data collection and entry tools for calculating unit costs using bottom-up and top-down approaches. These tools are color-coded for ease of use and include sheets for planning, data collection, and analysis.
